habitat: Woodland savanna; rarely montane forest. Nests in tall trees reused over years. Common summer-breeding brown eagle in Kruger (Newman's; SABAP1).
summary: A medium brown eagle and the most common brown eagle in Kruger in summer. Narrow parallel wings and a longish square tail held mostly closed. Feet, cere and gape yellow; eye dark. Several morphs including dark-headed and pale/white-headed birds (Newman's).

similar.note: Tawny is bulkier with broader wings and a shorter rounded tail; gape line differs from Wahlberg's slightly downturned gape (Newman's vs Lesser Spotted note).
Booted is smaller with white shoulder patch (pale morph) and translucent primary wedge (Newman's).
African Hawk-Eagle adult is boldly black-and-white below; immature brown can confuse (SABAP1).

research.note: Research confidence was medium-high and is stored as medium. No seasonal plumage change is described in the sources consulted, except presence/absence of migrants. Gaps: No juvenile/immature image in selected set. Structured marks keep the common form. The pale form is not a separate variant. Dark-headed and white-headed individuals also occur (Newman's). The schema has no morph field. Colour phrases outside the vocabulary were stored as the nearest swatch: dark to dark-brown.
